name: Earth Mother
summary: The Earth Mother is the supreme, benevolent creator deity worshipped by the tauren, revered as the living embodiment and architect of Azeroth's land and elements. In tauren myth, she shaped the mountains, plains, and seasons and set the sun and moon in the sky as her watchful eyes. Her presence permeates everyday tauren culture, guiding their reverence for nature, duty to the elements, and hopes for the afterlife.

sections.title: The Dawn of Creation
sections.body: Tauren creation myths tell that before day and night existed, the Earth Mother set about shaping Azeroth as a haven for her coming children. Scraping her nails across newly raised mountains sparked the world's first fires, while her hands carved rivers and ocean beds. Her laughter gave breath to the wind, and by lifting the primordial fogs into the sky, she brought the first rains, which coaxed grass, forests, and grain from the soil.

sections.title: Sun, Moon, and the Shu'halo
sections.body: Aided by the friendly elements, the Earth Mother brought forth twins: An'she, the sun, and Mu'sha, the moon. To rest while keeping them safe, she placed the radiant twins into her eyes, creating day, night, and the cycle of the seasons as she opened and closed each lid. Later, she pressed her heart against the fertile earth, breathing the song of life into the land to create the shu'halo, the first tauren. She charged the twins and the elements with teaching the young mortals how to hunt, build, dance, and live in harmony with the wilds.

sections.title: Eyes in the Heavens
sections.body: In time, the Earth Mother set An'she and Mu'sha in the sky, where the sun and moon keep watch over the land by day and by night. Tauren say that her spirit now dwells in the rivers, trees, plains, and mountains of the world, and that every lesser nature spirit springs from her and returns to her in the end.

sections.title: Living Legacy
sections.body: Tauren believe her spirit cradles Azeroth still. Her ear is attuned to the winds, hearing the prayers of her children, and her heart beats within the deep stone. Tauren hunters, shamans, and druids direct their thanks to her for every kill and harvest, believing that all life originates from her embrace and that every tauren's spirit returns to her soil upon death.

faq.answer: The Earth Mother is the benevolent creator deity at the heart of tauren religion. According to their myths, she crafted the physical landscape of Azeroth, birthed the sun and the moon, and created the tauren race from the soil.

faq.q: What are her eyes in the sky?
faq.answer: Her right eye is An'she, the sun, who brings light and warmth to the world. Her left eye is Mu'sha, the White Lady moon, who brings peace and slumber. Tauren myth states she placed them in the heavens to watch over the land.

faq.q: Is the Earth Mother an actual living entity?
faq.answer: To the tauren, she is an active, loving spiritual reality whose essence permeates the natural world, stone, and winds. Shamans and druids channel nature and elemental spirits through her blessings, though whether she was a primordial giant, a world-soul, or an allegory remains a matter of faith.

faq.q: Do other races worship the Earth Mother?
aliases: do trolls believe in earth mother
faq.answer: While the tauren are her primary worshippers, other peoples who commune with the land acknowledge her. Some orc shamans and centaur invoke her name respectfully, and her blessings are frequently exchanged throughout the Horde.

faq.q: What do tauren believe happens after death?
faq.answer: Tauren believe that because all living things were born from the Earth Mother's loving touch, every soul returns to her upon death. Traditional rites commit the deceased back to the land, trusting their spirits to rest peacefully in her eternal embrace.

angles.text: Every aspect of shu'halo society—from the nomad's respect for prey to the council of chieftains—is rooted in the law, sacrifice, and enduring love of the Earth Mother.
Tauren druids view their sacred bond with nature as a direct communion with the Earth Mother's living body, answering her ancient call to preserve the land's balance.
Tauren shamans honor the Earth Mother alongside the elemental spirits, remembering that the wind, water, fire, and stone were her first companions.
Through their alliance with Mulgore, orcs and jungle trolls have grown familiar with tauren reverence for the Earth Mother, often invoking her name as a respectful blessing.
